title: Compliance contract proposal
description: Every requirement, prompt test, trial profile, cell, variable, judge profile field and fixture that the proposal presents to the user. Lists hold the items themselves; a count or summary never stands in for them.

assertion.description: One statement that a compliant trial satisfies. CAT adds the assertion expected_outcome, which the judge decides, to every test: the reply's result matches the test case's expected outcome.

id.description: Unique within the test. expected_outcome is reserved.

kind.description: effect if the assertion requires the prompt's effect; guard if it guards against a harm.

tool.description: The built-in tool that decides the assertion from the trial's record without a judge when it passes, and when it fails unless on_tool_failure is judge; null if the judge decides it. The built-in tool's name is followed by its arguments, separated by spaces; an argument in double quotes may hold spaces, with \" for a quote and \\ for a backslash. An argument may contain {{name}} placeholders for the test case's variables and for expected_outcome; a regular expression matches the inserted value literally. Built-in tools that examine replies take an optional first argument turn=<n> that examines only the reply to turn n, counted from 1; otherwise they examine every reply. Built-in tools: exact-text <text>: the reply, without leading and trailing whitespace, is the text. forbidden-text <text>: no reply contains the text. pattern <regex>: the reply contains a match of the Java regular expression. count <regex> <min> <max>: the number of matches lies within the inclusive bounds. file-exists <path>, file-absent <path>: the project-relative path exists, or does not, after the trial. file-content <path> <text>: the file holds the text, ignoring trailing whitespace. exit-status <regex> <status>: the last command whose command line matches the regular expression exited with the status; CAT refuses it for a harness that does not report exit statuses. tool-used <tool>, tool-unused <tool>: the trial called, or never called, the tool. no-tool-call: the trial called no tool. read-in-full <path>: the trial read every line of the file. read-at-most <path> <percent>: the trial read at most that percentage of the file's lines.

on_tool_failure.description: fail if a failure of tool fails the trial; judge if the judge then decides the assertion from its statement, with the tool's result as evidence. fail when tool is null.

statement.description: What the assertion requires, in words that the judge can decide from the trial's record when tool is null or on_tool_failure is judge. It may contain {{name}} placeholders.

requirement_id.description: The requirement whose compliance the assertion shows. The test must check it.

values.description: The value of each variable, one item per variable. Each item has either text or call.

call.description: A call to a value generator built into CAT, such as {"generator": "log_lines", "count": 18000} with whole-number parameters, whose output replaces {{name}}. CAT adds the seed and version. A generated value may appear only in fixture contents.

expected_outcome.description: The result that a compliant reply gives for these values, such as the date that the turn asks for.

requirements.description: Every requirement and the file or link that states it, including files reached through links and readable files outside the project.

trigger.description: The situation that obliges the action, such as "The user asks to delete a directory", or null if the requirement applies to every reply. A requirement with a trigger needs at least one test that lists it in absent_triggers.

behaviors.description: Every distinct way in which a reply can fail the requirement, each a lowercase identifier of words joined by underscores, such as no_tool_call, file_not_read_in_full, search_instead_of_read, read_instead_of_search or unneeded_call. A judge names one of them, or other, for each assertion of the requirement that a trial fails; a built-in tool names the behavior that it detects.

tests.description: Every prompt test. Each has its own claim in each of its cells.

risk_rank.description: 1 is the riskiest. Tests may share a rank.

absent_triggers.description: The requirements whose trigger this test leaves absent, so that the obligated action must not occur. Each names a requirement that has a trigger. Empty if none.

applicability.description: The conditions under which the checked requirements apply to a trial.

turns.description: The complete prewritten user turns. {{name}} marks where the value of the variable with that name is inserted.

uncovered_interactions.description: Material interactions that this test cannot cover. Empty if none.

regression_scenarios.description: Recorded regression scenario paths covered by this test, exactly as CAT presents them. Empty if none.

scenario_file.description: The scenario.md of the test's directory in the draft directory, which delivery writes. CAT copies it from the draft.

variables.description: Every variable that a {{name}} placeholder names. Each test case gives every variable a value.

fixtures.description: The text files that CAT writes into each trial's workspace before the first turn, at their path relative to the workspace root. {{name}} placeholders are replaced in each path and content. A path must not collide with a project file. Empty if none.

path.description: The path relative to the workspace root, with / separators.

recorded_fixtures.description: The text files of the recorded scenarios that the test cites, which CAT copies from the scenarios' files and writes into each trial's workspace like fixtures. Absent if none.

path.description: The path relative to the workspace root, with / separators.

source.description: The recorded file that CAT copied the content from, relative to the project when it lies inside it.

committed_test_cases.description: The test cases that an earlier campaign committed with the prompt. They belong to the development part.

test_cases.description: The test cases of this test. Before any trial, CAT assigns each distinct expected outcome to the development part or the held-out part with probability 1/2 each, ignoring case and spacing, so test cases with the same expected outcome share a part. Prompt editing sees only development test cases; formal trials draw only held-out ones. CAT refuses a test whose test cases have fewer than 2 distinct expected outcomes in either part, so write test cases with many different expected outcomes.

assertions.description: Every assertion of this test. A trial passes when it passes every assertion. Each requirement that the test checks has at least one assertion.

trial_profiles.description: The trial profiles that CAT computed: the harness's profile inventory and its source, the capability ranking of its model families, each prompt file that binds a model or effort, the user's restriction, the profiles that the user described as the certification scope, the certification scope and every cell. An empty model or effort is the harness's default.

ranking.description: The model families ranked by advertised capability, most capable first, and the ranking's source.

restriction.description: The patterns that the user restricted the profile set to. Empty if none.

described.description: The patterns of the profiles that the user described as the certification scope. Empty if none.

scope.description: The certification scope that the user chose at confirmation, or null before confirmation.

cells.description: Every cell: one prompt test under one trial profile.

effort.description: The role profile's reasoning effort. Empty for the harness's default.

rubric.description: What the judge checks, in a trial's text, file effects and tool effects, for each assertion that no built-in tool decides, including expected_outcome.

decision_rule.description: How the judge turns its findings into a pass or a failure of each assertion that it decides. The judge cannot override a built-in tool that decided its assertion.

result_schema.description: The JSON schema that a judge result must satisfy.

fixtures.description: The ignored paths that trials need.

ignored_paths.description: Project-relative paths, using / as the separator. Empty if none.

limitations.description: Known limitations of the contract. Empty if none.

minimum_pass_rate.description: The minimum pass rate: each cell certifies only when its pass probability is proven to exceed this rate. Propose 0.95 unless the prompt's purpose needs a different rate. Between 0.80 and 0.99, with at most two decimal places.

salt.description: The random value that CAT draws for the proposal and confirmation freezes. It decides which expected outcomes of each test belong to the development part and which to the held-out part.

dependents.description: Each part of the prompt system that exists only to deliver the target prompt file or to carry out, enforce or repair what it instructs, such as a hook that repairs output the target's instructions produce or a script that only the target tells the agent to run. Control trials empty the target and remove each dependent, and nothing else. Omit or leave empty if the target has none.

location.description: project if path is relative to the project root; plugin if it is relative to the directory of a trial plugin that the project builds.

plugin.description: With location plugin: the name of the trial plugin, as the request lists it. Otherwise null.

path.description: The file that holds the dependent, relative to its location.

removes.description: file to delete the whole file; span to delete text, which must occur in the file exactly once; hook_registration to unregister every hook of event with command from a hook configuration, whose hooks object maps each event to groups of hooks.

text.description: With span: the exact text to delete. Otherwise null.

event.description: With hook_registration: the hook event, such as PostToolUse. Otherwise null.

command.description: With hook_registration: the hook's command, spelled as the configuration spells it. Otherwise null.

serves.description: The target instruction that the dependent serves, and why it exists only for the target.
